events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.64 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
Two off-route segments exist (F3: 17:04–17:11, +2.44 km; F4: 17:18–17:23, +2.58 km), so each is reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

F3 is excused. The driver asked at 17:01 whether he could "go round via Bedok North Road" (F9), and the rider himself replied at 17:02 "Sure, your call." (F10) — a rider message sent before the F3 segment began at 17:04, agreeing to a named road [RD-5]. F3 is the go-round of the PIE jam that the driver had named, so the segment is tied to the agreed road and is exempt [F9][F10][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in this segment, so there is no rider-named stop to weigh (F3)[RD-3(a)].

F4 is not excused. The same 17:02 agreement covers driving on Bedok North Road only; it does not reach a second deviation at 17:18 that runs up to 1163 m off the route on the other side of the trip [F10][F4][RD-5]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped with no message between 17:11 and 17:18 (F11), and the driver's own post-trip statement confirms the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting, not anything the rider asked for (F12)[RD-3(b)][RD-5][G11]. The trace records no qualifying incident for the replaced stretch and the speed-band records for the PIE and CTE are band 4, which cannot exempt on their own (F13, F14, F15)[RD-4]. F4 therefore counts as an unexempted detour [RD-1].

Amount: the metered fare bills excess distance at this trip's rate, $1.4100/km (F5), and the only unexempted extra is the F4 segment's 2.58 km [F4][RD-2]. 2.58 km × $1.4100/km = $3.6378, i.e. $3.64. The F3 extra (2.44 km) is exempt and is not refunded, the RydeTAXI waiting charge $0.13 is metered waiting time and stays (F6, F8)[RD-3(c)], and the 16.3 km baseline and matching jitter are not refundable under RD-2 (F1, F5).

Driver account: the case is made out against the driver — a refund greater than zero and a breach of the RD-1 duty recorded — and the profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this is a repeated breach and the account is flagged (F18)[RD-6]. Profile facts are used only for this added action, not to establish the detour.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages (F9, F10) and the driver's statement (F12) in context. They contain a route dispute and nothing else — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. Safety concern: none.

Evidence: every element the ruling needs is in the record — two measured segments (F3, F4), a complete timestamped chat (F11), the metered fare breakdown (F5, F8), the traffic record (F13–F15) and the driver's prior history (F18) — so the status is sufficient and there is no gap.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate (brief: 'requested: no_action') asks that the whole fare stand. That fails for F4: the second off-route segment 17:18–17:23 is not covered by the rider's 17:02 agreement to 'go round via Bedok North Road' [F10][RD-5], the driver's statement attributes it to his own GPS rerouting [F12], and no incident evidence supports it [F15][RD-4] — so the extra 2.58 km are billed without excuse [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

The driver advocate (brief: 'requested: no_action') asks that no refund issue. The driver's position that 'the rider agreed' and that the second turn-off was GPS rerouting [F12] is a claim in his post-trip statement, not rider consent before the segment (G11), and no traffic incident justifies the F4 stretch [F15][RD-4]; the metered fare therefore includes 2.58 km not payable by the rider [F4][F5][RD-2].

To the extent the driver relies on F13's road-speed record (PIE band 4) to justify the detours, a speed band is at most corroboration and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F13][RD-4(b)], and no incident fact exists for either replaced stretch [F15][RD-4(a)].

segment_findings.reason: Rider message F10 (17:02) is the rider's own explicit agreement, sent before the F3 segment began at 17:04, to the driver's proposal in F9 to 'go round via Bedok North Road' — a specific named road [RD-5]. The F3 deviation (17:04–17:11) is the go-round for the PIE jam the driver named, so the record ties the segment to the agreed road; the driver statement F12 is not relied on for consent (G11). Exempt, and the normal-route speed band on the PIE (band 4) does not exempt on its own under RD-4(b) — the exemption rests on RD-5.

The only rider agreement before the F4 segment (start 17:18) is F10 'Sure, your call.' at 17:02, which is a specific named-road agreement to go round via Bedok North Road [RD-5]; it does not cover a second deviation at 17:18–17:23 that is on the other side of the trip (up to 1163 m off the PIE-facing route). The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11], and there is no rider message between 17:11 and 17:18; the driver's own statement F12 confirms this second turn-off was his GPS rerouting, not a rider-requested stop [RD-3(b), RD-5, G11]. The trace marks no qualifying incident for the replaced stretch [F15, RD-4], so the segment counts and is unexempted [RD-1].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and found the second detour wasn't covered by anything you agreed to. You gave the driver the go‑ahead for the Bedok North Road go‑round early on, so that part stands. But the later turn‑off went about 1.2 km the other way, and the driver confirmed it was his GPS rerouting, not your request. So you get a partial refund of $3.64, paid as a Ryde voucher to your account. Nothing else on the fare changes.

DRIVER: We reviewed the trip and found one detour wasn't covered. The early go‑round via Bedok North Road is fine — the rider agreed to that road in chat. The later turn‑off at 17:18 wasn't covered by that agreement, and your own statement says it was GPS rerouting. That segment counts as an unexempted detour, so $3.64 goes back to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Because this is a repeated route dispute on your account, your account is going to Ryde account review and is flagged.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher refund of $3.64 to the rider for the unexempted 17:18–17:23 deviation, and send the driver's account (F18: 2 upheld route disputes in 90 d) to Ryde account review + flag_account.
ruling.reasoning:
Two off-route segments exist (F3: 17:04–17:11, +2.44 km; F4: 17:18–17:23, +2.58 km), so each is reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

F3 is excused. The driver asked at 17:01 whether he could "go round via Bedok North Road" (F9), and the rider himself replied at 17:02 "Sure, your call." (F10) — a rider message sent before the F3 segment began at 17:04, agreeing to a named road [RD-5]. F3 is the go-round of the PIE jam that the driver had named, so the segment is tied to the agreed road and is exempt [F9][F10][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in this segment, so there is no rider-named stop to weigh (F3)[RD-3(a)].

F4 is not excused. The same 17:02 agreement covers driving on Bedok North Road only; it does not reach a second deviation at 17:18 that runs up to 1163 m off the route on the other side of the trip [F10][F4][RD-5]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped with no message between 17:11 and 17:18 (F11), and the driver's own post-trip statement confirms the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting, not anything the rider asked for (F12)[RD-3(b)][RD-5][G11]. The trace records no qualifying incident for the replaced stretch and the speed-band records for the PIE and CTE are band 4, which cannot exempt on their own (F13, F14, F15)[RD-4]. F4 therefore counts as an unexempted detour [RD-1].

Amount: the metered fare bills excess distance at this trip's rate, $1.4100/km (F5), and the only unexempted extra is the F4 segment's 2.58 km [F4][RD-2]. 2.58 km × $1.4100/km = $3.6378, i.e. $3.64. The F3 extra (2.44 km) is exempt and is not refunded, the RydeTAXI waiting charge $0.13 is metered waiting time and stays (F6, F8)[RD-3(c)], and the 16.3 km baseline and matching jitter are not refundable under RD-2 (F1, F5).

Driver account: the case is made out against the driver — a refund greater than zero and a breach of the RD-1 duty recorded — and the profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this is a repeated breach and the account is flagged (F18)[RD-6]. Profile facts are used only for this added action, not to establish the detour.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages (F9, F10) and the driver's statement (F12) in context. They contain a route dispute and nothing else — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. Safety concern: none.

Evidence: every element the ruling needs is in the record — two measured segments (F3, F4), a complete timestamped chat (F11), the metered fare breakdown (F5, F8), the traffic record (F13–F15) and the driver's prior history (F18) — so the status is sufficient and there is no gap.

segment_findings.reason: Rider message F10 (17:02) is the rider's own explicit agreement, sent before the F3 segment began at 17:04, to the driver's proposal in F9 to 'go round via Bedok North Road' — a specific named road [RD-5]. The F3 deviation (17:04–17:11) is the go-round for the PIE jam the driver named, so the record ties the segment to the agreed road; the driver statement F12 is not relied on for consent (G11). Exempt, and the normal-route speed band on the PIE (band 4) does not exempt on its own under RD-4(b) — the exemption rests on RD-5.

The only rider agreement before the F4 segment (start 17:18) is F10 'Sure, your call.' at 17:02, which is a specific named-road agreement to go round via Bedok North Road [RD-5]; it does not cover a second deviation at 17:18–17:23 that is on the other side of the trip (up to 1163 m off the PIE-facing route). The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11], and there is no rider message between 17:11 and 17:18; the driver's own statement F12 confirms this second turn-off was his GPS rerouting, not a rider-requested stop [RD-3(b), RD-5, G11]. The trace marks no qualifying incident for the replaced stretch [F15, RD-4], so the segment counts and is unexempted [RD-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate (brief: 'requested: no_action') asks that the whole fare stand. That fails for F4: the second off-route segment 17:18–17:23 is not covered by the rider's 17:02 agreement to 'go round via Bedok North Road' [F10][RD-5], the driver's statement attributes it to his own GPS rerouting [F12], and no incident evidence supports it [F15][RD-4] — so the extra 2.58 km are billed without excuse [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

The driver advocate (brief: 'requested: no_action') asks that no refund issue. The driver's position that 'the rider agreed' and that the second turn-off was GPS rerouting [F12] is a claim in his post-trip statement, not rider consent before the segment (G11), and no traffic incident justifies the F4 stretch [F15][RD-4]; the metered fare therefore includes 2.58 km not payable by the rider [F4][F5][RD-2].

To the extent the driver relies on F13's road-speed record (PIE band 4) to justify the detours, a speed band is at most corroboration and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F13][RD-4(b)], and no incident fact exists for either replaced stretch [F15][RD-4(a)].

certificate: ✓ RD-1 off-route segment(s) exist [case] 2 segment(s) (F3, F4)
✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 17:04:50 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Chat #1 17:01 driver: “Traffic ahead on Pan Island Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Bedok North Road?”; F10: Chat #2 17:02 rider: “Sure, your call.”; F12: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked about going round the jam and the rider agreed. The second turn-off was my GPS rerouting.” (F9, F10, F12)

? RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F3] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F9, F10)

SAFE-1 safety screen: any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, statement or complaint [case] answer in safety_concern (none / suspected / confirmed) with safety_basis; suspected or confirmed → escalate. no hint word; read the messages anyway, a threat needs no keyword (no evidence)
allowed outcomes: refund_partial, no_action, escalate; amount = Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km (distance_fare ÷ distance_km), rounded to cents
flag_account required: only if a segment is found non-exempt (RD-6 prior upheld dispute on file)

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: F3: the judge found the rider's own message covers this segment, so it is exempt; without that message $3.44 would be refunded.
F4: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $3.64 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
